content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10-15 days of forecast horizon).
- Forecasts show upward trend bias, failing to account for mean reversion or downward corrections after spikes.
- Overshoots occur after sharp price increases; model lags in recognizing and adjusting for short-term volatility.
- Model underestimates true price drops in the second half of the forecast horizon, particularly after initial spikes.
- Forecasts tend to be smoother than actual price movements, missing abrupt reversals or corrections.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, especially when historical prices are trending upward.
- Correction should involve reducing forecast slope after spikes and introducing downward adjustments in later forecast periods.
